title: Correct magnitude expression
description: Essential: Student must provide the final magnitude as f = (1+√3)/2 μmg or its decimal equivalent.

title: Correct direction statement
description: Essential: Student must state the frictional force is perpendicular to the paper plane, pointing outward.

title: Normal force decomposition
description: Important: Student must correctly resolve gravity into components perpendicular to both AB and BC surfaces.

title: Friction on each surface
description: Important: Student must calculate kinetic friction separately for each contact surface using f = μN.

title: Force superposition
description: Important: Student must sum the two frictional forces as vectors along the same direction.

title: Angle identification
description: Optional: Student correctly identifies the relevant angles (60° and 30°) from the geometry.

title: Direction misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly states direction as along groove, upward, or inward rather than outward perpendicular.

title: Wrong normal force
description: Pitfall: Student uses mg directly as normal force on one or both surfaces without proper decomposition.

title: Vector addition error
description: Pitfall: Student attempts to add frictional forces as perpendicular vectors instead of parallel ones.
